narrative.intro: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $11.6B in federal contract spending in FY2026 to date. The agency executed 6,879 awards with an average award size of $1.7M. Obligations fell 26.4% year over year. Historical obligations show FY21 at $15B, FY22 at $15.2B, FY23 at $16.1B, FY24 at $15B, FY25 at $15.8B, and FY26 at $11.6B. Research and development in the physical, engineering, and life sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) is the largest category at $4.5B. Guided missile and space vehicle manufacturing follows at $1.8B. The top vendors include CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY at $1.8B and THE BOEING COMPANY at $1B, with other major contractors such as THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC at $477M and LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP at $400M. This snapshot shows where NASA is concentrating contract dollars and which firms capture the largest shares through FY2026 to date.

sections.heading: How much did the agency obligate in FY2026 to date?
sections.body: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $11.6B in FY2026 to date. The agency made 6,879 awards with an average award size of $1.7M. Obligations fell 26.4% year over year compared with the prior period. Prior fiscal-year totals were $15B in FY21, $15.2B in FY22, $16.1B in FY23, $15B in FY24, and $15.8B in FY25.

sections.heading: What are the top contract categories and who are the largest vendors?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) led categories at $4.5B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing accounted for $1.8B, with other notable categories including Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) at $701M and Engineering Services at $684M. CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY and THE BOEING COMPANY are the top two vendors at $1.8B and $1B respectively. THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC, LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP, and NORTHROP GRUMMAN SYSTEMS CORPORATION follow at $477M, $400M, and $370M respectively.

faq.q: How much does National Aeronautics and Space Administration spend on contracts?
faq.a: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $11.6B in contracts in FY2026 to date. The agency issued 6,879 awards with an average award size of $1.7M, and obligations fell 26.4% year over year. Historical annual obligations were $15B in FY21, $15.2B in FY22, $16.1B in FY23, $15B in FY24, and $15.8B in FY25.

faq.q: What does National Aeronautics and Space Administration buy?
faq.a: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration buys a mix dominated by research and development and space manufacturing. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounts for $4.5B, Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing accounts for $1.8B, and other major categories include Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) at $701M, Engineering Services at $684M, and Industrial Building Construction at $518M.

faq.q: Who are National Aeronautics and Space Administration's largest contractors?
faq.a: The largest contractors for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration are CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY and THE BOEING COMPANY. CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY received $1.8B and THE BOEING COMPANY received $1B, followed by THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC at $477M, LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP at $400M, and NORTHROP GRUMMAN SYSTEMS CORPORATION at $370M.
